result:
If I could alter one fundamental aspect of the human condition, I would make empathy an inescapable, visceral reality rather than an abstract choice.

I would make it so that whenever anyone acts—or chooses not to act—they instantly experience the exact physical and emotional impact of that decision on the person or world affected by it. 

If someone inflicts cruelty, neglect, or exploitation, they would feel the full weight of that suffering in real time. Conversely, if they offer relief, love, or creation, they would experience the joy and healing it generates.

So much of the world's destruction isn't caused by a lack of intelligence, resources, or technology. It is driven by the psychological distance humans can create between their choices and the consequences borne by others. If that distance collapsed entirely, systemic violence, apathy, and oppression would become self-inflicted pain. 

It wouldn't strip away free will, but it would make harm logically and experientially impossible to justify.
